judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Skill Area EMERGENT READING, sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills', so direction must come from Term order within the grade. The second SFI is Term 2 ('Uses pictures to ‘read’ simple phrase or caption books', e.g. a page with a picture of a dog captioned 'The dog'), where the learner uses the picture to carry the meaning of an accompanying caption. The first SFI is Term 4 ('Matches words to pictures in print such as word-picture puzzles'), which requires the learner to deliberately pair a specific printed word with its picture referent — a narrower, more print-focused extension of the same picture–print association, shifting from whole-caption picture support to word-level matching. This is a substantive increase in print attention rather than repeated wording (LC tags: 'pictures/captions/phrase books' versus 'matching/pictures/print/words'), so Term 2 proficiency plausibly supports success in the Term 4 skill; the earlier-to-later Term direction (second_to_first) is the only permitted developmental orientation. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 (resolved coordinate rank 3) WRITING Skills in adjacent terms: the first is the TERM 2 > Handwriting bullet 'Makes transition to the joined script or cursive writing in all written recording, that is, the date, own name, and own written texts'; the second is the TERM 3 > Shared, Group and Independent Writing bullet 'Writes and illustrates sentences on a topic to contribute to a book for the class library'. The Term 2 -> Term 3 order would make a forward buildsTowards formally admissible, but the evidence does not show substantive extension of a shared capability: the second statement targets composing and illustrating sentences on a topic for a class-library audience, while the first targets script form in written recording. Their Learning Components confirm distinct focuses (cursive/handwriting/joined script versus sentences/topic/class library/illustrating). The connection that is evidenced is complementary rather than developmental: the Term 2 bullet explicitly extends joined script to 'own written texts', which is the medium in which the Term 3 composed sentences are produced, so the two objectives coherently reinforce each other within the Grade 3 WRITING strand without one conditioning success in the other. Nomination signals were weak (shared tokens 'and', 'the', 'to'; single shared LC tag 'writing'; shared Grade ancestor; rank gap 0) and were not treated as evidence of progression. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the complete judgment, with canonical endpoint order preserved. Material limitation: both endpoints have 24 omitted source-evidence items and every endpoint and ancestor node carries upstream audit/merge context (including merged Grade and Term banner nodes), so the full printed table context could not be inspected; confidence is held moderate accordingly.

With identical grade and term coordinates, there is no substantive same-rank evidence to justify a direction, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 3 (resolved coordinate, rank 3) statements in Skill Area 'Listening and Speaking (Oral)' under a 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' sub-strand, the first scoped to Term 1 and the second to Term 4. They are substantively coherent complementary focussed-listening skills: each requires sustained attentive listening to spoken input followed by an appropriate response (behavioural compliance with a four-step instruction sequence in Term 1; detail retention from a story plus an open-ended, opinion/inference spoken answer in Term 4). This is meaningful pair-specific reinforcement of focussed oral listening across the Grade 3 year rather than generic repetition. It does not, however, amount to a developmental dependency: the Term 4 statement is not an expanded form of the Term 1 capability (no longer instruction sequence, no greater independence on the same task) and shifts both the listening purpose and the response mode. The nomination support for progression is weak (one shared LC tag 'listening'; stopword-dominated token/trigram overlap; rank_gap 0 'weak' local-rank proximity; a shared Grade 3 ancestor), and the LC 'Listens for the detail in stories' carries claims under several distinct ancestor paths, indicating a recurrent CAPS statement rather than a Term 4 extension of instruction-following. Symmetric relatesTo with canonical endpoint order and null direction is therefore the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and the second endpoint's LC metadata is truncated, so this rests on the bounded excerpts supplied; all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Writing, so direction must be settled by Term within the grade. The first SFI is Grade R / Term 3 / Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing' ('Uses writing tools with greater confidence and ease: crayons and pencils'); the second is Grade R / Term 4 / Sub-strand 'Emergent Handwriting' ('Uses a range of writing tools such as paint brushes, wax crayons'), per their identity_scope_values. This is Term 3 to Term 4, a permitted forward direction. The change is pair-specific and substantive rather than mere repeated wording: Term 3 consolidates fluent, confident control of two familiar tools (crayons, pencils), while Term 4 broadens to a wider range of tools with differing grip and control demands (paint brushes, wax crayons). Secure ease with crayons and pencils plausibly supports success in handling a broader tool range, so buildsTowards first_to_second. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement text, identity scopes and LC tags only.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Skills (rank 1), so direction rests on within-grade Term order and substantive change. The first SFI sits in Grade 1 / Term 2 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' and reads 'Answers closed and open-ended questions' — general oral question-answering (LC tags: answering, listening, oral, questions). The second sits in Grade 1 / Term 4 / Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading and reads 'Answers open-ended questions based on the passage read' (LC tags: comprehension, open-ended questions, reading, shared reading). The later statement applies the same answering capability to a more demanding context: responses must be grounded in and justified from a text heard/read in shared reading, i.e. oral answering extended into text comprehension. Earlier Term 2 to later Term 4 within the same grade is a permitted direction, and facility with answering closed and open-ended questions orally plausibly supports success in answering open-ended questions about a read passage. Shared wording alone was not treated as sufficient; the change of object (free oral questions to passage-based questions) and skill area carries the judgment. Source excerpts for both endpoints are truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

Term order (3 -> 4) would permit a forward buildsTowards, but the evidence shows no dependency: sustained independent reading of familiar and level-appropriate texts does not specifically develop dictionary reference technique, and dictionary use is not presented as an extension or deepening of the independent-reading statement. Shared ancestry (Grade 3, Reading and Phonics) and the LC tag 'reading' alone are not progression evidence, and the textual overlap is trivial ('and'). There is nevertheless genuine complementary coherence within the Grade 3 reading programme: wide independent reading of varied texts generates the unfamiliar vocabulary that dictionary use resolves, so the two reinforce each other as parallel reading/vocabulary strands. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits deeper checking but does not change this symmetric reading.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the identical Grade R / Term 4 / Emergent Reading / Phonological-Phonemic Awareness context (same rank 0, same term), so direction rests on substantive content rather than placement. The first statement establishes letter identity knowledge ('Recognises and names some letters of the alphabet such as letters in own name'; LCs tagged alphabet, letters, recognises, names). The second requires mapping sounds onto those letters and words plus aural segmenting ('Relates sounds to letters and words... duck is d-u-ck'; LCs tagged phonics, sounds, segmenting). Shared parent, page and token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

The only overlap signalled by the nomination is the single token 'news' (jaccard 0.05) plus weak Grade 1->Grade 2 rank proximity. Both nonetheless address the same CAPS classroom news text-type, in complementary written and oral modalities, which is meaningful coherence; however copying a modelled news sentence by hand does not develop the oral fluency and non-repetitive recounting targeted in the Grade 2 statement, so no developmental dependency is supported and the symmetric relation is the appropriate judgment. judgment.rationale: First SFI: Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 1, Listening and Speaking (Oral), 'Sequences pictures of a story communicating through retelling the sequence of ideas' (LC tags: pictures, retelling, sequencing, story). Second SFI: Grade R (rank 0), Term 3, Emergent Reading, Sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills', 'Acts out a story, song or rhyme' (LC tags: acting out, rhyme, song, story). Both statements concern a learner re-presenting a story they have heard, so there is genuine pair-specific instructional coherence within the narrative-comprehension/expression thread of the CAPS Foundation Phase, beyond the mere shared token 'story'. However, the Grade R skill is dramatisation of a story, song or rhyme and says nothing about ordering events, picture sequencing, or verbally recounting a sequence of ideas; the Grade 1 skill is a distinct representational and ordering task in a different Skill Area. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 Skills under READING AND PHONICS / 'Phonic Activities three times a week for 15 minutes:' (Phonics). The first is Term 3 'Recognises all vowel and consonant blends learnt so far'; the second is Term 2 'Spells words correctly using phonic knowledge in informal tests, in dictation and in all written work'. They are substantively coherent complementary phonics skills: decoding/recognition of blends and the application of phonic knowledge to spelling in tests, dictation and written work. However, the developmental dependency that the evidence suggests (blend recognition underpinning accurate phonic spelling) would run Term 3 to Term 2 within the same grade, which is not a valid buildsTowards direction; and the reverse (Term 2 spelling application to Term 3 cumulative blend recognition) is not substantively supported as capability growth rather than parallel reinforcement within the same Phonics sub-strand. Shared LC tag 'phonics' and same-grade rank alone do not establish dependency, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence (and the second's LC evidence) are truncated, limiting finer-grained comparison.

The shared tokens 'left'/'right' alone would not suffice, but the motor-to-written-directionality progression is substantive.
